rows.description: Parents see the change and feel hurt, afraid for their child or ashamed before relatives. Listening with curiosity, not alarm, protects the relationship whichever way the belief goes.
graph_context: previous stage: First questions
next stage: Anger or emptiness
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: fear, shame, curiosity, doubt

rows.description: Some feel anger at what they were taught, others a hollow quiet where meaning used to sit. Both are part of the honest process, and rushing to a firm conclusion does not end them.
graph_context: previous stage: Doubt and distance
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: anger

rows.description: A mentor or elder meets a young person's questions with interest, says that honest doubt is old and common, and does not use shame or fear. Being allowed to ask keeps the relationship and often the faith.
graph_context: next stage: Doubt and distance
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: fear, shame, interest, doubt

rows.description: The person reads texts, talks with thoughtful believers and sceptics and tests ideas against experience. Serious seeking accepts uncertainty and treats hard questions as worth their time.
graph_context: next stage: A changed relationship with belief
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: doubt

rows.subtype: Stage 6: A changed relationship with belief [Actor]
rows.description: Some return to their tradition with a chosen, more personal faith, some adopt another path and some settle in non-belief with values intact. Each is a legitimate outcome of honest searching.
graph_context: previous stage: Wrestling and seeking
next stage: Living with respect and peace
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Stage 7: Living with respect and peace [Response]
rows.description: The person keeps ties with family, joins rituals for love if not for creed where they wish, and neither mocks belief nor pressures others. Peace comes from honesty and mutual respect, not from winning the argument.
graph_context: previous stage: A changed relationship with belief
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: affection, admiration, calm

rows.description: A friend of another belief listens to a seeker without trying to convert them or score points. Being accompanied, not argued with, is what a person in doubt needs most.
graph_context: next stage: A changed relationship with belief
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: doubt

rows.description: A new employee sees a colleague backdate a form or trim a test to meet a target and is told it is how things work. The first bend feels harmless, and the pressure to fit in outweighs the unease.
graph_context: next stage: Normalising

rows.description: The shortcut is repeated by many, and the team makes jokes about it. Because everyone does it, it starts to seem acceptable, and the unease fades.
graph_context: previous stage: A small shortcut
next stage: Euphemisms and rationalising

rows.description: Fraud becomes creative accounting, and a hidden defect becomes a known limitation. Softer language and stories about protecting jobs let people avoid seeing what they are doing.
graph_context: previous stage: Normalising
next stage: Pressure and loyalty
